issues.evidence: WebFetch proxy: 'web-fetch budget for this session is exhausted'; https://exeter.gov.uk/planning-services/pre-application-enquiries/local-validation-checklist/ 'failed at its site (client_error)'

issues.detail: All 6 tab_items are boilerplate or fragments, not requirements. They are: a privacy notice; file-format rules (5Mb, PDF, 200 dpi) run together with the start of the Location Plan text; a list of guidance links plus phone and email contacts that ends partway into '4.11 Designing Out Crime Statement'; 'Secured By Design ... Devon & Cornwall Police contact:'; a ProPG noise guidance citation; and a list of environmentally sensitive sites that runs on into the '3.1 Householder Application (Contents page)' heading.
issues.evidence: 'Any personal information provided will be used by us...'; 'please call 01392 265223 or email planning@exeter.gov.uk'

issues.detail: Householder shows '(none)' (national requirements only), yet the document has its own '3.1 Householder Application' checklist table, which Grokbot never parsed. Several local triggers in the extracted text are location-based and would catch householder schemes: an Ecology Report – Bats and Birds for sites within or next to an environmentally sensitive area, archaeology for groundworks in the Area of Archaeological Importance, and heritage. The same applies to the other application-type sections (Outline, Reserved matters, Advertisement, Prior approval and so on), which are all recorded as '(none)'.
issues.evidence: tab_items: '... Exeter Valley Park. 8 3.1 Householder Application (Contents page) National Requirements Document / Plan etc.'

issues.detail: Requirements named in Grokbot's own extract that have no app_type row: Designing Out Crime Statement (4.11; Secured by Design / Devon & Cornwall Police); Ecology Report – Bats and Birds (as its own item); Noise Impact Assessment (ProPG cited); Green Infrastructure Statement (Core Strategy CP16). Green Infrastructure appears only under the wrong label 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans'.
issues.evidence: '4.11 Designing Out Crime Statement (Contents page)'; 'Ecology Report – Bats and Birds'; 'Green Infrastructure Statement National Planning Policy Framework 180 Core Strategy Policy CP16'

issues.detail: Several triggers belong to a different requirement. 'Fire Statement' and 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' both carry 'Development which is major development (except engineering or mining operations, material changes in use, or waste development)', which is the Design and Access Statement trigger; a Fire Statement depends on building height or storeys with dwellings, and an ES on EIA screening. 'Heritage Statement' and 'Flood Risk Assessment' carry 'Development on sites within or adjoining an environmentally sensitive area (see page 8)', which is the ecology trigger. 'Advertisement drawings' carries the Air Quality Assessment text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' carries the arboricultural method statement text. 'Cycle parking details' carries the roof plans text. 'Ventilation / Extraction' carries the site sections text. 'Coal Mining / Land Stability' carries the LVIA text and contact details.
issues.evidence: Fire Statement excerpt: '...When Required? Development which is major development (except engineering or mining operations, material changes in use, or waste development)'

issues.detail: Many other triggers are jumbled table headers or cut-off fragments. Air Quality Assessment: the real triggers appear elsewhere in the extract ('All applications for major development, except car-free residential development' and 'sites within 20 metres of the AQMA'), but the excerpt mixes in an exemption for disabled access works. Archaeological Assessment: mixes in CIL form names and repeat-application fee text, when its trigger is groundworks in the Area of Archaeological Importance. Daylight/Sunlight and Ecological Survey: identical header jumble. CIL form: garbled. Design and Access Statement: only lists the legal sources. Ground investigation: 'suitably qualified geotechnical, civil or structural engineer.' Structural Survey: 'civil or structural engineer.' Planning Obligations: 'All 41 Document / Plan etc.' Open space: quotes an NPPF paragraph instead of the trigger.
issues.evidence: Planning Obligations excerpt: 'Discharge of Planning Obligations) Regulations 1992 (as amended) When Required? All 41 Document / Plan etc.'

issues.detail: 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' and 'Fire Statement' are placed under 'Minerals & waste (county)'. Exeter City Council is not the minerals and waste planning authority (Devon County Council is), and the quoted text actually excludes mining and waste development. Separately, the advertisement drawings and illumination requirement sits under Full planning while Advertisement consent says '(none)'.
issues.evidence: '(except engineering or mining operations, material changes in use, or waste development)'

issues.detail: 32 of the 38 Full-planning rows are marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. Many apply more widely: Flood Risk Assessment, ecology, heritage, archaeology and tree survey are location-based. Others are major-only or apply to specific types, such as the Waste Audit Statement and Sustainability/Net Zero Carbon Statement (major development) and the Viability Assessment (where CP7 affordable housing is not met). 'Floor plans / Elevations' sits under Listed building consent and Lawful development certificate with an unrelated, garbled trigger.
issues.evidence: notes: 'INFERRED: application type not named in extracted text of a general local list; placed under Full planning - check source for applicability'

issues.detail: 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is encouragement, not a validation requirement.
issues.evidence: 'We encourage all applicants to take advantage of our pre-application service before making a formal application.'

issues.detail: Identical trigger text is reused for different requirements: Roof plan and Cycle parking; Arboricultural Impact Assessment and Schedule of works; Daylight/Sunlight and Ecological Survey; Fire Statement and Environmental Statement.
issues.evidence: Roof plan and Cycle parking both: 'Roof plans are required for all applications for new, replacement or extended buildings...'

summary: The live source could not be checked because the web budget was exhausted, so whether the list is current is unknown. Even from Grokbot's own extract, the Exeter capture is poor: the tab items are boilerplate, many triggers belong to other requirements, the Householder and other type-specific tables (section 3) were never parsed, and EIA and Fire Statement are wrongly filed under county minerals and waste.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The list date 2024-07-01 is a guess from the file name ('july-2024'), not an adoption or publication date in the document or page text. Grokbot also read a committee decision (ieDecisionDetails ID=2261) but did not use it for the date.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The month is supported by the document itself, not only the file name: the cover reads "Local List ... July 2024" and the version table has "V1 12.07.2024". The date basis should be text rather than url, and the exact date is 12 July 2024.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
